Japanese characters brushed in black sumi ink, arranged in three separate vertical columns read from right to left. The columns occupy the broad central writing area of the horizontal scroll and are distributed evenly across its width. Each complete column fits comfortably inside the paper without touching the cloth border, rollers, or margins.

The calligraphy is executed in a formal upright brush hand of the samurai period. The ink is matte black, slightly grey where the brush ran dry, and has bled very slightly into the paper fibres at the beginning of each stroke.

EXPOSURE, this is the whole look
The frame is exposed for the sky and everything else falls one and a half stops under it. Most of the image sits in the lower third of the value range. The sky is the brightest thing in the picture and it is still a middle dark blue, never pale and never white. The four corners are one stop darker than the centre, so the frame closes in on the head.

WHAT STAYS DARK
The black robe is a solid mass. Only the top edge of the shoulder and the rim of the collar separate from it, and everything below the shoulder line dies into near black with no weave, no folds and no texture visible. The skin of the nape and the rim of the ear are only just readable, lit to the point where you can tell they are skin and no further. The pale linen reads as a soft middle grey-blue, never white.

WHAT CATCHES LIGHT
The oiled hair is the brightest thing on any body in the frame: fine individual strands, with one narrow band of sheen across the knot. The wet palm resting on the shoulder has a narrow bright edge around the fingers. Those two are the only highlights in the whole image.

LIGHT
The only light in the scene is the sky itself, a flat overcast dome at the end of blue hour, coming from above and slightly behind them. There is no sun disc, no lamp, no hard shadow and no cast shadow on the ground.

COLOUR
The whole image sits on one single hue, a deep desaturated blue. Skin, wool, linen and rock all read as that same blue, because the sky is the only thing lighting them. Separation comes from brightness alone. The shadows go to a dense blue-black.

THE HAND
The palm is wet. Where it rests, the black wool darkens further and holds the shape of the hand.

STAINS
Every stain has soaked through the cloth from underneath and spread along the weave, so its edges are irregular and feathered and its centre is darker than its rim. The cloth is stiffened where it has dried.

DEPTH
The two men are fully sharp. Mountain ridges on the horizon sit at roughly 8 percent contrast, only a fraction darker than the sky, half swallowed by the air.

AIR
Heavy still haze fills the field behind them at about 30 percent density, thickening with distance.

FINISH
Shot on a long lens, 18 degrees field of view, from chest height. Fine 35 mm grain, slightly heavier in the shadows. 2K.

SURFACES
Every surface in frame is plain: bare wool, bare linen, bare skin, bare sand, bare sky. No writing, no emblems, no patterns anywhere. Both men are adults.

A group reference plate of infected people in ordinary night street clothes soaked with rain, standing upright with their bodies working perfectly, faces slack and eyes focused on nothing. INFECTED APPEARANCE, and this must be frightening on sight, a horror film and never a crowd of extras: the whites of their eyes are drowned in solid red, every capillary burst, the irises clouded to a blind milky grey, the pupils blown huge and fixed, and none of them blinking. Their eye sockets are sunken into black hollows and ringed with bruised purple. Their faces are skeletal, the cheeks caved in under the cheekbones, the skin drained to a grey-white wax, damp with sweat and blotched with dark purple pooling under the jaw and along the neck, and darkened to near black around the eyes, the nostrils and the mouth. Webs of swollen black veins spread from the corners of their eyes across the temples and stand out along their throats like cords. Their lips have shrivelled back and gone black, the gums receded and blackened so the teeth look far too long, and thick saliva hangs in strings from open jaws, pink and foaming at the corners. They all turned MINUTES ago, so every mark on them is FRESH AND WET: blood still glistening and running from the corners of their mouths down their chins and throats, wet and bright under the light, and at the collar each shirt is torn open over the bite that turned them, the fabric around it soaked dark and shining, the bites themselves hidden under torn cloth and never shown. Their hair is matted and stuck to sweating scalps. Their heads are tilted at wrong angles, the neck tendons standing out hard, the shoulders pushed forward, their bodies coiled to launch and never at rest, and their hands held in half-curled claws with blackened broken nails. Their clothes are torn at the collar and the sleeves and soaked with WET dark stains that still catch the light, never dry and never crusted. Lighting is hard and unkind, raking so the hollow sockets and the caved cheeks fall into black shadow. NO open wound, NO torn flesh, NO exposed bone, NO fresh or running blood, NO prosthetic monster mask and NO fantasy creature: these are human beings whose bodies still work perfectly and whose persons are gone. Every face is invented. WARDROBE OF THE CROWD, described head to foot so the mass stays consistent: on the head, most of them bare-headed with wet flattened hair and a few in plain knitted caps, nothing branded and nothing written; at the waist, ordinary belts and plain waistbands on jeans and work trousers, some coats hanging open and unbelted; on the feet, ordinary street shoes and boots, wet through and dulled with rain, no bare feet anywhere; and what is carried over the outfit sits on the LEFT shoulder or the LEFT side in the few who still have a bag or a coat over one arm, while most carry nothing at all. They press along the dull brass rail of a theatre box, each turned a different way with the heads turning, none of them oriented together, moving constantly and searching. Skin keeps its pores, its sweat and the flush of physical effort; technical fabric keeps its weave and its worn edges. Sodium street light and headlights are the only sources. No illustration, no 3D render, no animation, no painterly texture, no plastic skin. STORYBOARD FRAME, a single still that stands for one shot of a film. Photoreal live-action still from a physical cine camera, 21:9 widescreen, exactly as the finished film will look. It is a FRAME OF THE FILM, not an illustration, not a sketch, not a comic panel and not a drawing: no lines, no ink, no pencil, no cel shading, no panel border and no caption.

THE MOMENT THIS FRAME HOLDS: ALREADY MID-ATTACK. The dark-green swordsman cuts high at the head; it is turned aside. He cuts low at the knee; turned aside.

LENS AND POSITION, matched to the shot: spherical prime at 35mm, at the chest height of a standing man, handheld, riding the blades.

FRAMING LAW: a fighter's head is never cropped by any edge. Duel framing runs from mid-thigh to a hand's width above the head, so legs, torso, the crossing blades and BOTH FACES sit in the same frame. Kneeling framing runs from the knees to above the head. NEVER legs alone, NEVER feet alone, NEVER an empty landscape with nobody in it.

LOOK: one rule governs every frame, a world with no colour in it and one saturated colour that lives only in cloth, 90 to 10. The 90 carries no chroma: pale raked sand, undyed linen, dark robes and the pine line read as one neutral scale from bone white to near-black. The 10 is the deep madder red of set-in staining in cloth. Skin keeps its own low warmth. No fourth colour.

LIGHT: natural daylight only, one source and it is the high midday sun, almost overhead and a little behind camera, out of frame so its disc is never seen. Every shadow is SHORT and hard-edged and sits directly under the brow, the nose and the jaw. The sand goes to near-white where it faces up and the shade under the pine wall closes to true black, four stops between them. The air is clean and empty, no mist and no haze. A weak second bounce comes back up off the pale sand into the underside of every face. No fill, no rim light, no lens flare.

GLASS: spherical primes, f/2.8, physical cine lens, 180 degree shutter motion blur, fine 35mm grain, no halation.
